3d1ad756cd0dd95edb8349a1d5be4879c323450c.summary: Intel 471 blog post on the January 2021 law enforcement takedown of the Emotet botnet, announced by U.S. and European agencies. The post says several Ukrainian nationals were allegedly arrested over running the botnet's infrastructure. It judges the long-term impact uncertain, notes that infected machines may carry Qbot or Trickbot that could be used to regain control, and says any rebuild would be easy to detect.

3d9466227e0af020d117e0fa6e53dad68738555b.summary: Threatpost reported in March 2017 that two recent fileless malware campaigns against financial institutions, government agencies and other enterprises, disclosed by Kaspersky Lab and Cisco Talos, were linked by Morphisec to the same attack group. Morphisec found the delivery framework on a command and control server, which the attacker took down after brief contact with the researchers. Kaspersky Lab said the Meterpreter attacks could be connected to the GCMAN and Carbanak groups, and FireEye calls the group FIN7.

3d761dea89536bf0c182f222cbed4ca34fa59848.summary: eSentire TRU reports April 2024 incidents in which FIN7, a financially motivated group active since 2013, used sponsored Google Ads and fake brand websites to deliver signed MSIX installers. The installers dropped NetSupport RAT, which led to a Python-based loader that injected DiceLoader and set up scheduled-task persistence. The report says these cases resemble earlier FIN7 MSIX activity described by Microsoft and Red Canary, citing a similar PowerShell script and similar infrastructure patterns. Recommended controls include EDR, phishing awareness training, and AppLocker controls on MSIX…
